Convergence can be slow for high-order scattering media (many interactions) or highly anisotropic media, requiring many samples or variance reduction techniques like Next Event Estimation (NEE) [S2][S5, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that Monte Carlo methods take a long time to converge for high-order scattering or highly anisotropic participating media (Source [S2]). It further notes that these scenarios require many samples to converge to a smooth result due to the stochastic nature of the simulation (Source [S5]). Additionally, Source [S2] lists Next Event Estimation (NEE) as an advanced approach used to improve the convergence rate, and Source [S5] confirms that NEE is used to reduce variance and speed up convergence, particularly in media with high scattering coefficients.
